results: The exact auxiliary Dirichlet characteristic of a diagonal source is odd at EVERY complex L2 lift. At every nonzero frequency, the analytic order of the full H-minus-one scalar Dirichlet characteristic at z^2-c equals the ACTUAL auxiliary Dirac operator algebraic multiplicity. Both extended and natural analytic orders are proved; no simple-root hypothesis is used in this transport.

Canonical auxiliary Dirichlet branches retain the SAME original signed index, exact scalar energies zeta_n^2-c, actual physical boundary spectrum and the full L2 lattice-displacement sequence. For EVERY complex shifted L2 Miura lift, one cutoff gives actual SIMPLE scalar Dirichlet zeros on both signed tails.

For a real original H-minus-one potential and literal real shifted Miura lift, every sufficiently high positive scalar Dirichlet branch lies between the SAME intrinsic original periodic Hill endpoints, including collapsed pairs. Its complex norm deviation from the exact physical midpoint is at most one half the original gap norm.

Auxiliary operator counting isolates every sufficiently distant canonical auxiliary characteristic zero in its original free disc. The entire positive real interval between the corresponding periodic Dirac endpoints stays in that disc. Squaring the positive real root therefore proves EXACTLY ONE scalar Dirichlet zero in every sufficiently high intrinsic original Hill gap, including collapsed gaps.

The high-gap uniqueness theorem is proved for EVERY real original H-minus-one potential with NO caller-supplied lift: a real shifted L2 Miura lift is constructed inside the proof. The resulting unique-root assertion is stated entirely in the potential, full Dirichlet characteristic and intrinsic original periodic labels.

A shared coefficient lemma proves that squaring any L2 displacement from a signed complex lattice loses exactly one bracket weight, including a constant energy translation and the central index. Applied to the actual canonical auxiliary branches, their scalar energies have inverse-bracket weighted L2 displacement from n^2*pi^2 at the SAME signed index, for EVERY complex lift.

A shared original-source theorem transports ALL real ordinary boundary root algebraic multiplicities through the verified source phase. Every actual auxiliary root at real type has algebraic multiplicity one, including its finite central block and collapsed periodic gaps.

For EVERY real original H-minus-one potential, EVERY zero of its full scalar Dirichlet characteristic has analytic order ONE and NONZERO spectral derivative. A constructed real Miura lift avoids zero square-root energy at the given root; the actual auxiliary multiplicity-one theorem then includes all low scalar energies without exception.

A shared analytic inverse-function argument CONSTRUCTS a local analytic scalar zero selection from a nonzero partial derivative on a complex Banach parameter space. Consequently every simple full H-minus-one Dirichlet zero, and hence EVERY zero at EVERY real original potential, extends to an actual local analytic Dirichlet-energy branch under arbitrary sufficiently small COMPLEX H-minus-one perturbations.
qualifications: Analytic-order transport at nonzero square-root frequency is exact for all complex potentials and all multiplicities. The scalar characteristic-to-auxiliary identity itself includes zero frequency, as proved previously. Constructed real lifts avoiding that frequency prove all-real-potential scalar simplicity without excluding ANY physical energy.

All-real-potential SIMPLE ZEROS here means analytic multiplicity of the independently constructed full scalar characteristic. Its native source scalar operator-domain matching is not yet proved, so scalar operator algebraic simplicity is not yet claimed by substituting the auxiliary operator.

The signed auxiliary branch energies are actual simple scalar zeros outside a proved finite central block. The energy values assigned to central auxiliary indices are not asserted to be the ordered central scalar Dirichlet sequence. No fake central scalar labels are introduced.

The intrinsic high real-gap theorem constructs the needed lift internally and states unique existence of an actual scalar characteristic zero using only q and its intrinsic periodic Hill endpoints. The high-gap half-length bound includes collapsed gaps, but its real-potential scope is explicit.

The n-times-L2 asymptotic is proved as inverseBracketCoefficients(n)*(energy_n-(pi*n)^2) in ell2. This is the original bracket weight, with no frequency rescaling. It applies to the full signed branch sequence, but no global central scalar ordering is inferred from that auxiliary ordering.

Local analytic root branches are CONSTRUCTED in the full complex H-minus-one norm, starting from every real-potential Dirichlet zero, including low energies. No canonical root selection or unproved continuity of such a selection is assumed.
